articles.title: Nine in Ten Indian Adults Have Abnormal Cholesterol, Landmark ICMR Study Finds
articles.excerpt: The ICMR-INDIAB study of 23,665 adults reveals 87.3% have at least one lipid abnormality, with an estimated 355 million affected even without diabetes, obesity, or hypertension.
articles.image_caption: Cardiovascular disease is now the leading cause of death in India, responsible for more than a quarter of all fatalities. The ICMR-INDIAB study found 87.3 per cent of Indian adults have at least one abnormal lipid level.
articles.nri_angle: The 2018 ACC/AHA guidelines classify South Asian ancestry as a cardiovascular risk-enhancing factor, meaning Indian Americans should discuss early lipid screening with their doctors even without traditional risk markers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bee Venom Boosts Standard Parkinson's Therapy in New Mouse Study
articles.excerpt: Researchers at the University of Guadalajara found that combining bee venom with L-DOPA/carbidopa improved both motor and cognitive outcomes in a Parkinson's disease model, outperforming the standard drug alone.
articles.nri_angle: The research could eventually inform new treatment options for the estimated one million Parkinson's patients in India and diaspora communities affected by the disease.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: UK Backs Two Non-Invasive Tests to Cut Nine-Year Endometriosis Diagnosis Wait
articles.excerpt: NICE recommends Endotest and EndoSure for NHS primary care use, potentially ending the invasive surgery requirement that has left millions waiting years for answers.
articles.nri_angle: South Asian women in the UK face diagnosis delays averaging 11 years due to cultural and systemic barriers; these new primary care tests could disproportionately benefit ethnically diverse communities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Monsoon Fever Season Pushes Indian Doctors to Urge Early Lab Testing
articles.excerpt: As dengue, malaria, typhoid and other infections surge across India during peak monsoon, health experts stress that timely blood tests are critical to accurate diagnosis and avoiding antibiotic misuse.
articles.nri_angle: Indian diaspora members visiting family during monsoon season should be aware of regional fever risks and get tested promptly if symptomatic.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Eli Lilly's Triple-Agonist Drug Hits 22.6% Weight Loss, Clearing Path to FDA Filing

articles.nri_angle: Indian Americans face disproportionately high rates of type 2 diabetes and obesity, making next-generation weight-loss treatments directly relevant to diaspora health.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Regular Exercise Erases Half of Muscle Aging's Molecular Signature, Study Finds
articles.excerpt: A multiomics study published in Nature Aging found that physically trained older adults retain youthful gene expression profiles in skeletal muscle, with 50% of age-related molecular differences absent compared to their sedentary peers.
articles.image_caption: Older adults participate in a strength training session. A new study published in Nature Aging found that regular exercise reverses roughly half of the molecular aging signature in skeletal muscle.
articles.nri_angle: Health and fitness advice relevant to all readers; Indian diaspora increasingly focused on preventive health and longevity.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Traffic Noise May Raise Parkinson's Risk by 64 Percent, Dutch Study Finds
articles.excerpt: A study of over 50,000 people in the Netherlands found that living with high levels of road traffic noise was independently associated with increased Parkinson's disease risk, adding to growing concerns about noise pollution as a neurological hazard.
articles.image_caption: Heavy traffic on an urban road in India. A Dutch study of 150,000 people found that living near persistent traffic noise raises Parkinson's disease risk by up to 64 percent, with Indian cities routinely exceeding WHO noise limits.
articles.nri_angle: Indian cities are among the noisiest in the world; health implications for diaspora who grew up near heavy traffic
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: New Breathalyser Detects Fat Burning in Real Time From a Single Breath
articles.excerpt: Researchers at ETH Zurich have developed a handheld device that measures breath acetone with laboratory-grade accuracy in 90 seconds, offering a new way to track metabolism during exercise, fasting, and dieting.
articles.image_caption: The Nutrion breathalyser, developed by ETH Zurich spin-off Alivion AG, measures acetone levels in exhaled breath. Researchers validated the device against laboratory mass spectrometry in a study published in the journal Device.
articles.nri_angle: Non-invasive metabolic monitoring could benefit India's 100-million-plus diabetic population and health-conscious diaspora tracking fitness and fasting regimens.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Monsoon Health Myths Indian Doctors Want You to Stop Believing
articles.excerpt: From the idea that antibiotics fix every fever to the misconception that mosquitoes only breed in dirty water, doctors are debunking dangerous monsoon myths as seasonal infections spike across India.
articles.image_caption: A person navigates monsoon rains in India. Indian doctors say common beliefs about monsoon health — from avoiding curd to shunning exercise — are myths that can actually harm well-being during the rainy season.
articles.nri_angle: Many diaspora families share monsoon health advice across WhatsApp groups — knowing which tips are myths could prevent misguided self-treatment during visits home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Endometriosis Affects 190 Million Women. Science Is Finally Catching Up.
articles.excerpt: A landmark genetic study and new diagnostic tools are reshaping the understanding of a disease that has been chronically underfunded and dismissed for decades.
articles.image_caption: Endometriosis affects an estimated 190 million women worldwide. New diagnostic tools and treatments are finally bringing the condition out of the shadows.
articles.nri_angle: Endometriosis research breakthroughs and funding shifts could improve care access for the global Indian diaspora, where cultural stigma around menstrual health often compounds diagnostic delays.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Most Americans Retire Earlier Than Planned and Wish They Had Saved More
articles.excerpt: A new TIAA Institute report finds 52% of retirees left the workforce before they expected, with three-quarters regretting they didn't start saving sooner.
articles.image_caption: A growing body of research shows that most Americans retire earlier than planned, often due to health issues or job loss, and wish they had saved more.
articles.nri_angle: Indian Americans planning long careers in the U.S. face the same early-retirement risks; the TIAA data underscores the importance of maximizing 401(k) contributions and planning for retirement scenarios well before age 65.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: GLP-1 Weight Loss Drugs Linked to Higher Risk of Hair Loss, Studies Find
articles.excerpt: University of Pennsylvania researchers found users of drugs like Ozempic and Mounjaro faced up to 68% higher odds of alopecia, though absolute rates remain low at 3 to 9 per 1,000 patients per year.
articles.image_caption: An Ozempic injection pen manufactured by Novo Nordisk. A University of Pennsylvania study published in The BMJ found GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic are associated with up to 68% higher risk of hair loss compared to other diabetes medications.
articles.nri_angle: GLP-1 drugs are widely used among the Indian diaspora for weight management and diabetes, making this hair loss finding directly relevant to treatment decisions for this population.

articles.title: Too Much Protein? These Warning Signs Say It's Time to Ease Up
articles.excerpt: As protein-fortified products flood supermarket shelves and high-protein diets dominate social media, nutritionists warn that consistently exceeding your body's protein needs can cause real health problems — from kidney strain to unexplained weight gain.
articles.image_caption: Protein supplements come in many forms including powders, bars, and shakes. Nutritionists warn that exceeding recommended daily intake can cause digestive and kidney issues.
articles.nri_angle: Indian diaspora households increasingly adopting Western protein-heavy diets and supplements may be overshooting their needs, particularly when traditional Indian diets with dal, paneer, and legumes already provide adequate protein.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Fatty Liver Disease Now Affects One in Three Adults Worldwide — and Most Don't Know It
articles.excerpt: The silent epidemic of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease is surging globally, with India among the hardest-hit countries. New treatments and screening tools offer hope, but experts warn early detection remains critically low.
articles.image_caption: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) now affects an estimated one in three adults globally. Early detection through routine screening can prevent progression to cirrhosis.
articles.nri_angle: South Asian populations face heightened risk due to genetic susceptibility to insulin resistance and metabolic syndrome at lower BMIs, making proactive liver screening essential for diaspora Indians.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Overusing Powerful Antibiotics While Millions Lack Basic Medicines, Lancet Study Finds
articles.excerpt: A first-of-its-kind global framework covering 186 countries reveals nearly all nations prescribe too many high-risk 'Watch' antibiotics. India's consumption is especially skewed, with broad-spectrum drugs dominating while essential first-line treatments remain underused.
articles.image_caption: Antibiotic pills and capsules in a pharmacy setting. A major Lancet study found 99% of countries overuse broad-spectrum antibiotics that drive drug resistance.
articles.nri_angle: The routine overprescribing of antibiotics in Indian healthcare settings affects global resistance patterns that cross borders with travellers and trade, directly impacting the Indian diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: World Sjögren's Day: What the Indian Diaspora Should Know About This Underdiagnosed Autoimmune Disease

articles.title: Two New NHS Tests Could Slash Endometriosis Diagnosis Time From Nine Years to 45 Minutes

articles.excerpt: Fampridine, a twice-daily pill that improves walking speed in up to 43 percent of patients, becomes available on the NHS in England from Thursday — years after Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.

articles.nri_angle: The approval is relevant to the large Indian diaspora population in the UK, where MS affects over 120,000 people in England alone and the drug will now be available without private prescription costs.

articles.title: Arizona Confirms First Clade I Mpox Case as U.S. Infections Rise
articles.excerpt: The travel-associated case adds to more than 20 Clade I mpox infections reported across the United States since late 2024, though health officials say the risk to the general public remains low.

articles.nri_angle: The rising number of travel-associated Clade I mpox cases in the U.S. is relevant for diaspora communities with frequent international travel between the United States, South Asia, Africa, and Europe.

articles.title: Inside Amitabh Bachchan's Fitness Routine at 83: Pranayama, Plant-Based Diet, and a Mindset His Trainers Call Unmatched

articles.title: Swimming Eases Chronic Low Back Pain, Landmark Australian Study Finds

articles.title: Nearly Half of Indian Doctors Use AI in Practice, Yet 69% Say They Want to Quit Medicine
articles.excerpt: A striking paradox in Indian healthcare: doctors are embracing technology faster than almost any other profession, but burnout, low pay, and systemic dysfunction are driving a mass exodus urge.

articles.title: A Spoonful of Peanut Butter Before Bed Could Help You Sleep, Says US Physician

articles.title: Spouses of Dementia Patients Face Up to Sixfold Higher Risk of Developing the Disease

articles.title: Your Thymus May Decide How Long You Live, Two Major Studies Find
articles.excerpt: Harvard-led research published in Nature reveals the long-overlooked chest gland strongly predicts longevity, cardiovascular risk, and cancer immunotherapy outcomes in adults.
articles.image_caption: A CT scanner of the kind used in the Harvard-led studies that analyzed thymic health in more than 27,000 adults. The research linked thymus condition to longevity and cancer immunotherapy outcomes.
articles.nri_angle: Immunotherapy use is expanding rapidly across India's cancer centres and among diaspora patients; thymic health scores could eventually help clinicians personalise treatment for Indian-origin patients worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Last Iron Lung Users Are Gone, but Polio Still Isn't
articles.excerpt: With the deaths of Paul Alexander and Martha Lillard, the iron lung era has ended in the United States — yet experts warn that the virus remains a global threat, particularly as vaccine hesitancy grows.
articles.image_caption: Paul Alexander in his iron lung in 1986. He contracted polio at age six in 1952 and spent the next 72 years in the device, becoming the Guinness World Record holder for longest time in an iron lung.
articles.nri_angle: India eliminated polio in 2014 through a massive vaccination campaign — a public health triumph the diaspora can take pride in. But with wild poliovirus still circulating in neighboring Pakistan and vaccine hesitancy growing globally, the story remains unfinished.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Heart Attacks in Your 20s and 30s: Why India's Young Are Dying of a Disease Their Grandparents Survived
articles.excerpt: Cardiologists warn that half of all heart attacks in Indian men now occur before the age of 50, driven by a toxic combination of sedentary lifestyles, chronic stress, and genetic predisposition.
articles.image_caption: A young man getting a health checkup. Cardiologists warn that heart attacks among Indians aged 20-30 are rising 2% annually.
articles.nri_angle: South Asian immigrants in the US and UK face 2-4x higher coronary disease rates than the general population. Cardiologists recommend screening by age 30 for Indians abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: America's GLP-1 Drug Use Surges as Semaglutide Dominates and Costs Climb
articles.excerpt: A new study finds GLP-1 receptor agonist use grew by 230% among diabetics and 643% among non-diabetics between 2017 and 2022, with semaglutide driving the boom — but total per-person spending is rising even as out-of-pocket costs fall.
articles.image_caption: YouTube / Minute USA

Journal of Managed Care and Specialty Pharmacy

articles.title: Minoxidil: The Go-To Solution for Hair Growth
articles.excerpt: Exploring the surge in popularity of minoxidil among those facing hair loss.
articles.image_caption: minoxidil

articles.title: Drinking Up to Five Cups of Coffee a Day May Lower Stroke and Diabetes Risk, Major Study Finds
articles.excerpt: An umbrella review of over 100 meta-analyses finds consistent evidence that moderate coffee consumption is associated with reduced risk of several chronic diseases, though experts caution results vary by preparation method.
articles.image_caption: A cup of freshly brewed coffee. A comprehensive review of over 100 meta-analyses found that moderate coffee consumption is linked to reduced risk of stroke, type 2 diabetes and several other chronic conditions.
articles.nri_angle: India is one of the world's largest coffee-producing nations, and filter coffee is integral to South Indian culture; the findings are relevant to diaspora communities who maintain these traditions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Filtered Coffee Linked to Slower Biological Aging While Instant Coffee Shows Opposite Effect
articles.excerpt: A UK Biobank study of nearly 50,000 people found divergent associations between coffee brewing types and biological aging markers, with inflammation as a possible mediating pathway
articles.image_caption: A pour-over coffee setup with a glass carafe and paper filter. A new study found that filtered coffee was associated with slower biological aging compared to instant coffee.
articles.nri_angle: For South Indian diaspora households where filter coffee is a daily ritual, the study offers modest reassurance about their preferred brewing method.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: PCOS Renamed PMOS as Landmark Study Links Condition to Four-Fold Higher Heart Disease Risk
articles.excerpt: A new Lancet study shows women with the condition formerly known as PCOS face quadruple the risk of cardiovascular disease, adding urgency to a global push for better screening and earlier intervention.
articles.image_caption: A woman undergoes a health screening at a medical facility. New research links PMOS, the condition formerly known as PCOS, to a four-fold increase in cardiovascular disease risk.
articles.nri_angle: One in five Indian women is affected by PMOS, making this renaming and the new heart disease data directly relevant to millions in the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: People With Type 2 Diabetes Face Up to 25 Times Higher Risk of Severe Dengue, Review Warns
articles.excerpt: A comprehensive review highlights that diabetic patients who contract dengue for the first time face dramatically worse outcomes, a finding with urgent relevance as India enters peak monsoon season.
articles.image_caption: A close-up of a mosquito feeding on human skin in Bilaspur, India. Research shows people with type 2 diabetes who contract dengue for the first time face dramatically higher odds of developing severe disease.
articles.nri_angle: India has the world's second-largest diabetes population and sees hundreds of thousands of dengue cases annually, making this finding critical for NRIs visiting family during monsoon season.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A 10-Minute Walk After Meals Can Slash Blood Sugar Spikes, and Experts Say Indians Need It Most
articles.excerpt: Multiple studies show a short post-meal walk lowers glucose levels more effectively than a single long workout, a habit that could help the millions of Indians at risk of Type 2 diabetes.
articles.image_caption: A person walks along a path after a meal. Research shows that even a leisurely 10-minute stroll within 30 minutes of eating can significantly reduce post-meal blood sugar spikes.
articles.nri_angle: Indians are genetically predisposed to Type 2 diabetes and develop it a decade earlier, making post-meal walking habits especially relevant.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Night Owls Carry More Belly Fat and Higher Blood Sugar, Major Study Finds
articles.excerpt: A study of nearly 300 women published in Frontiers in Nutrition links evening chronotype to poorer metabolic health, higher body fat percentages, and less nutritious food choices — even when total calorie intake is similar.
articles.image_caption: A woman works on her laptop late at night. New research links being a night owl to higher body fat, elevated blood sugar, and poorer metabolic health markers.
articles.nri_angle: The findings are relevant for the Indian diaspora, where long working hours and late-night eating patterns are common, and where diabetes and metabolic syndrome rates are already elevated.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Fatty Pancreas Now Recognised as a Disease, Linked to Diabetes and Cancer Risk
articles.excerpt: An international panel of experts has formally classified fatty pancreas as a distinct disease entity, establishing a clinical framework that connects pancreatic fat accumulation to type 2 diabetes and pancreatic cancer.
articles.image_caption: An anatomical illustration of the human pancreas and surrounding organs. International experts have formally classified fat accumulation in the pancreas as a distinct disease linked to diabetes and cancer.
articles.nri_angle: The classification has significant implications for Indians, who face among the world's highest rates of type 2 diabetes and are increasingly affected by metabolic syndrome at younger ages.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: AI Can Spot Pancreatic Cancer Up to 16 Months Before Doctors, Johns Hopkins Surgeon Says
articles.excerpt: A Johns Hopkins researcher highlights advances in AI-powered cancer detection that could transform outcomes for one of the deadliest cancers, while a new vaccine shows promise in intercepting the disease.
articles.image_caption: A medical professional reviews diagnostic imaging on a screen. Johns Hopkins researchers are developing AI tools that could detect pancreatic cancer up to 16 months earlier than human readers.
articles.nri_angle: Pancreatic cancer disproportionately affects South Asians; AI-driven early detection breakthroughs at institutions like Johns Hopkins could improve outcomes for the Indian diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Excessive TV Watching in Midlife Linked to Brain Shrinkage and Memory Loss, New Study Finds
articles.excerpt: Researchers found that frequent television viewers in their 40s and 50s showed smaller brain volumes and greater white matter damage decades later — and exercise alone may not offset the risk.
articles.image_caption: A medical professional examines a brain scan on a monitor. New research links excessive midlife TV watching to reduced brain volume in areas associated with memory.
articles.nri_angle: Evening TV watching is deeply embedded in Indian family routines; findings suggest simple lifestyle adjustments could protect brain health.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Gets Its First Multi-Cancer Blood Test as Dr Dangs Lab Partners With Zydus and Guardant Health
articles.excerpt: The Shield test can screen for 10 common cancers from a single blood draw, marking a significant step toward early detection in a country where most cancers are diagnosed at advanced stages.
articles.image_caption: A laboratory technician processes blood samples for diagnostic testing. Dr Dangs Lab has become the first laboratory in India to offer Guardant Health's multi-cancer detection blood test nationwide.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs with family in India can now access advanced multi-cancer screening through a simple blood test, potentially enabling early detection for parents and relatives back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Cervical Cancer Cases in India Drop 37% Over a Decade, Driven by Screening and Vaccination Push
articles.excerpt: Data from India's cancer registries shows a significant decline in cervical cancer incidence rates over the past decade, as opportunistic screening expands and the country rolls out its first nationwide HPV vaccination campaign.
articles.image_caption: A healthcare worker administers a vaccine. India launched its first nationwide HPV vaccination campaign in February 2026, targeting 11.5 million adolescent girls to combat cervical cancer.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora families can help counter vaccine hesitancy among relatives in India and should be aware that HPV vaccination is now freely available at government facilities for 14-year-old girls nationwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Shamita Shetty Opens Up About Endometriosis, Surgery, and the Two Years It Took to Lose 5 Kg
articles.excerpt: On Soha Ali Khan's podcast, the actor described sudden weight gain, pain that woke her from sleep, and a diagnosis that came only after years of dismissed symptoms.
articles.image_caption: Shamita Shetty at a public event. The actor recently spoke about her endometriosis diagnosis and recovery on Soha Ali Khan's podcast All About Her.
articles.nri_angle: Endometriosis affects roughly 10 percent of women of reproductive age globally, yet stigma around discussing menstrual health persists in many South Asian communities, making public conversations like this particularly valuable for diaspora audiences.

articles.title: Artificial Sweeteners Linked to Faster Memory Decline, Major Study Finds
articles.excerpt: An eight-year study of over 12,700 adults found that consuming common artificial sweeteners was associated with cognitive decline equivalent to 1.6 years of brain aging, particularly in people under 60.
articles.image_caption: Artificial sweeteners found in diet sodas and sugar-free products are under increasing scientific scrutiny
articles.nri_angle: Health awareness for health-conscious Indian diaspora communities where sugar alternatives have become increasingly popular as part of weight management and diabetes prevention strategies.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Brain Health Crisis Deepens as Neurologist Shortage Leaves Millions Without Care
articles.excerpt: With 80 times fewer neurologists per capita than wealthy nations and 3.5 million new cases of neurological disability each year, India's growing brain disorder burden is straining an already overstretched healthcare system.
articles.image_caption: A medical professional reviews a brain scan at a hospital. India's neurologist shortage has left millions without access to specialist neurological care.
articles.image_credit: Photo by cottonbro studio on Pexels
articles.nri_angle: Rising brain disorder rates in India affect diaspora families with aging parents back home who may struggle to access neurological care in smaller cities and rural areas.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A 10-Minute Morning Yoga Routine You Can Do Without Leaving Your Bed
articles.excerpt: From bridge pose to spinal twists, experts say a brief stretch sequence in bed can reduce stiffness, boost energy, and set a positive tone for the day.
articles.image_caption: A woman practices a gentle yoga stretch on her bed during a morning routine. Research shows that even 10 minutes of morning yoga can reduce stress, improve mobility, and boost energy levels throughout the day.
articles.nri_angle: Morning yoga draws from centuries of Indian tradition. For diaspora Indians balancing demanding careers abroad, a brief bed-based routine offers a low-barrier way to stay connected to wellness practices rooted in their heritage.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Andhra Villagers Hold Frog Weddings to Pray for Rain as State Faces 48% Rainfall Deficit
articles.excerpt: As El Niño squeezes India's 2026 monsoon to its weakest in 11 years, communities across Andhra Pradesh are reviving the centuries-old Mandooka Parinaya ritual, marrying frogs in elaborate ceremonies to invoke the rain god Varuna.
articles.image_caption: A frog perched on a wet surface. Villagers across drought-hit Andhra Pradesh are performing the ancient Mandooka Parinaya ritual, marrying frogs in traditional ceremonies to invoke the rain god amid a severe monsoon deficit.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora members with family in drought-prone Andhra Pradesh and Telangana face concerns about agricultural livelihoods and water scarcity affecting relatives, while the frog wedding tradition offers a cultural touchstone connecting NRIs to their rural roots.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Where to Buy Authentic Kanjivaram Sarees in India: A Complete Guide

articles.title: CDC Staff Cuts Leave US Struggling to Contain Largest Cyclospora Outbreak on Record
articles.excerpt: The parasitic disease lab shrank from 11 people to three after USAID funding was axed, slowing the federal response as more than 7,000 Americans fell ill from contaminated lettuce.
articles.image_caption: Fresh iceberg lettuce at a market. The CDC and FDA have traced the ongoing cyclospora outbreak to shredded iceberg lettuce sourced from central Mexico and supplied by Taylor Farms de Mexico.
articles.nri_angle: Indian Americans who regularly consume salads and fresh produce should be aware of the 27-state lettuce recall, particularly Walmart Marketside-brand products, as the outbreak's scale raises broader food safety concerns for all US residents.

articles.title: India's Medical Tourism Market Crosses $20 Billion as Patient Arrivals Triple Since 2020
articles.excerpt: Driven by cost savings of up to 80%, expanding visa access and stronger safety standards, India is rapidly closing the gap with Thailand and Singapore as a global healthcare destination.
articles.image_caption: A doctor at a Fortis hospital in India stands in front of advanced diagnostic equipment. India now has over 1,299 NABH-accredited hospitals serving international patients.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs and their families increasingly use India's medical tourism infrastructure for elective and complex procedures, benefiting from dramatic cost savings and improved safety standards compared to Western healthcare systems.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Why Indians Get Diabetes a Decade Earlier — and the Mental Health Link Making It Worse
articles.excerpt: New research reveals that genetic beta-cell dysfunction, a carb-heavy diet, and an overlooked diabetes-depression feedback loop are driving India's epidemic into younger age groups — with implications for the diaspora worldwide.
articles.image_caption: A glucometer and testing supplies used for blood glucose monitoring. India now has over 100 million adults living with diabetes, with a growing share diagnosed before age 40.

articles.nri_angle: NRIs traveling to India during monsoon season now have a proactive vaccination option against dengue, available without prior infection testing.

articles.title: Extreme Heat Is Crushing India's Workers: Lost Wages, Broken Bodies, and a Crisis With No Safety Net
articles.excerpt: A new global report warns that heat stress could erase nearly 24 workdays per year for outdoor workers in South Asia by 2030, while India's garment factory study finds 87% of workers suffering heat-related symptoms.

articles.image_caption: A researcher works with test tubes in a laboratory setting. India's draft health policy proposes expanding multidisciplinary research units across medical colleges nationwide.

articles.image_caption: Walking at a brisk pace has been linked to lower risks of heart disease and cognitive decline in multiple studies.

articles.title: AI-Assisted Colonoscopy Shows Promise for Lynch Syndrome but Falls Short of Breakthrough
articles.excerpt: The largest randomized trial of artificial intelligence in Lynch syndrome colonoscopy found that current AI tools do not significantly improve detection rates when used by expert endoscopists, though they show potential for spotting hard-to-see flat lesions.
articles.image_caption: A surgeon performs an endoscopic procedure in an operating room. Researchers are testing whether AI-assisted colonoscopy can improve cancer detection in patients with Lynch syndrome.

articles.title: Creatine May Supercharge Immune Cells That Fight Cancer, UCLA Study Finds
articles.excerpt: The popular fitness supplement energized dendritic cells that direct the body's cancer-killing T cells, slowing tumor growth in mice and pointing to potential applications in immunotherapy and cancer vaccines.
articles.image_caption: Protein supplement powder being added to a shaker. UCLA researchers found that creatine, widely used by athletes, may also help the immune system fight tumors.
articles.nri_angle: Creatine is one of the most widely used supplements among fitness-conscious diaspora communities. The finding that it may have anti-cancer properties adds a new dimension to its established role in exercise performance.

articles.title: Weight-Loss Drugs Linked to Higher Frailty Risks in Older Adults, Major Study Warns
articles.excerpt: A large-scale analysis of nearly 55,000 patients found that GLP-1 drugs like tirzepatide carry elevated risks of muscle wasting, malnutrition and dehydration in seniors, just as U.S. Medicare expands access to the medications.
articles.image_caption: Medical supplies including a syringe and tape measure on a white surface. A new study underscores the trade-offs between weight loss and lean tissue preservation in patients taking GLP-1 drugs.
articles.nri_angle: With rising obesity rates among Indian Americans and growing interest in GLP-1 medications, the findings have direct implications for diaspora communities managing weight with these drugs.

articles.excerpt: With private school costs rising 10 to 12 percent annually and coaching expenses nearly matching tuition by secondary school, Indian families are caught between aspiration and affordability.

articles.nri_angle: South Asians carry genetic predispositions that make them more vulnerable to stress-related glucose dysregulation, with India's 89.8 million diabetics and 43% undiagnosed rate making this a deeply personal issue for the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Archana Puran Singh Adopts Strict Ayurvedic Routine After 15-Day Bengaluru Retreat
articles.excerpt: The 63-year-old actor and Kapil Show regular has cut sugar, maida, and fried food from her diet, now eats dinner at 7 PM and sleeps by 10 PM after completing an Ayurvedic wellness programme.
articles.image_caption: Archana Puran Singh at a public event in 2024. The veteran actor recently completed a 15-day Ayurvedic wellness retreat in Bengaluru.
articles.nri_angle: Ayurvedic wellness retreats in India are attracting rising interest from NRIs reconnecting with traditional health practices, with centres in Karnataka, Kerala, and Goa reporting increased bookings from overseas visitors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Dementia Risk Factors Vary Sharply Across Countries, Lancet Study Finds
articles.excerpt: A new analysis of 214,000 older adults across 14 countries reveals that while the risk factors for dementia differ dramatically by region, they cluster in strikingly similar patterns worldwide.
articles.image_caption: A doctor holds an elderly patient's hands during a consultation. A new cross-national study finds that dementia risk factors like education, obesity, and hypertension vary sharply across 14 countries.
articles.nri_angle: Indian immigrants may carry distinct lifetime risk profiles shaped by conditions in India, where low education and vision loss dominate dementia risk, rather than the obesity and social isolation patterns common in Western countries.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ankita Konwar Becomes First Assamese Woman to Cross the English Channel, Learned to Swim Just Three Years Ago
articles.excerpt: The endurance athlete and wife of fitness icon Milind Soman completed the iconic Dover-to-Calais crossing as part of an international relay team, marking the 100th anniversary of the first woman's Channel swim.
articles.image_caption: An open-water swimmer cuts through the waves wearing a bright swim cap. Ankita Konwar completed the English Channel relay crossing on July 3, becoming the first woman from Northeast India to achieve the feat.
articles.nri_angle: Konwar's journey from non-swimmer to Channel crosser in three years celebrates extraordinary Indian achievement and Northeast Indian representation on the global stage.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Why Summer Sunshine Alone Won't Fix Vitamin D Deficiency — Especially for South Asians
articles.excerpt: A new UK study finds vitamin D levels barely improve even in summer for older adults and people with darker skin. For Indians — at home and in the diaspora — the problem runs deeper than a lack of sunlight.
articles.image_caption: Sunlight streaming through a natural setting. A new study finds that summer sunshine alone is insufficient to correct vitamin D deficiency for older adults and people with darker skin.
articles.nri_angle: South Asians face compounding risk factors for vitamin D deficiency — darker skin pigmentation, northern-latitude living and vegetarian diets — making year-round supplementation essential.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Cyclospora Parasite Outbreak Sickens Thousands Across the US With Taco Bell Lettuce Under Scrutiny
articles.excerpt: More than 5,100 possible cases of cyclosporiasis have been reported across 30 states, with shredded iceberg lettuce from a Mexican supplier linked to infections at Taco Bell.
articles.image_caption: Fresh lettuce leaves displayed at a grocery store. Federal investigators have linked shredded iceberg lettuce from a Mexican facility to a cyclosporiasis outbreak affecting more than 5,100 people across the United States.
articles.nri_angle: Directly affects Indians living in the US who eat at chain restaurants and buy produce from major grocery stores.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kerala's Monsoon Flu Crisis: 4,405 Influenza Cases and 49 Deaths in 2026
articles.excerpt: Kerala is grappling with a severe influenza outbreak driven by H1N1 and other strains as monsoon season intensifies, with the state recording the highest flu-related fatalities among all communicable diseases this year.
articles.image_caption: A healthcare worker prepares medical supplies at a clinic. Kerala's public health infrastructure has been mobilized across all districts to manage the influenza surge during the 2026 monsoon season.
articles.nri_angle: The outbreak poses a direct concern for the large Keralite diaspora, many of whom travel home during the monsoon season. Health experts advise travelers to India's southern states to get vaccinated before visiting and take standard respiratory precautions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ozempic and Cancer: Why the Promising Headlines Outpace the Science
articles.excerpt: More than two dozen studies presented at a major oncology conference suggest GLP-1 drugs may reduce cancer risk, but researchers warn the evidence is observational and clinical trials are still needed.
articles.image_caption: A semaglutide injection pen, the active ingredient in Ozempic and Wegovy. Researchers are investigating whether GLP-1 drugs may have anti-cancer properties beyond their established metabolic benefits.
articles.nri_angle: South Asian communities face elevated diabetes and metabolic syndrome rates, making GLP-1 drug findings on cancer risk especially relevant for India and the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Approves Wegovy for Fatty Liver Disease in New Milestone for GLP-1 Drugs
articles.excerpt: India's drug regulator has cleared Novo Nordisk's semaglutide injection for treating MASH, a serious form of fatty liver disease that affects roughly two in three Indians, making it the first GLP-1 drug approved for this condition both globally and in India.
articles.image_caption: A medical professional prepares a syringe for injection. Wegovy is administered as a once-weekly subcutaneous injection using a prefilled pen device.
articles.nri_angle: South Asians are disproportionately susceptible to metabolic liver disease, and the approval gives family in India access to a treatment previously limited to Western markets.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
